Vertices of an oriented ellipse

Source: R/plotting.R
ellipse_points.Rd

Computes the outline of an ellipse defined by its centre, the length of its semi-major axis, its aspect ratio, and the azimuth of its long axis. The coordinate system is assumed to be map-like: x points east and y points north.

Usage

ellipse_points(x0, y0, a, R, angle, n = 100)

Arguments

x0, y0

Numeric. Coordinates of the ellipse centre.

a

Numeric. Length of the semi-major axis (the full long axis is 2 * a).

R

Numeric. Aspect ratio of the ellipse, \(R = a / b\), where b is the semi-minor axis. Must be \(\ge 1\).

angle

Numeric. Azimuth of the long axis in degrees, measured clockwise from geographic north (i.e. from the positive y axis). Because an axis has no direction, angle and angle + 180 describe the same ellipse.

n

Integer. Number of vertices used to draw the outline.

Value

A data.frame with n rows and columns x and y. The first and last vertices are the same, so the outline is closed.

Details

The long-axis unit vector is \((\sin\phi, \cos\phi)\) and the short-axis unit vector is \((\cos\phi, -\sin\phi)\), where \(\phi\) is angle in radians. The points are $$\mathbf{p}(t) = \mathbf{c} + a\cos t\,\mathbf{u} + b\sin t\,\mathbf{v}, \quad t \in [0, 2\pi].$$

Examples

# Long axis N-S: y-range is +/- 1, x-range is +/- 0.5
p <- ellipse_points(0, 0, a = 1, R = 2, angle = 0)
range(p$x); range(p$y)
#> [1] -0.4999371  0.4999371
#> [1] -0.9994965  1.0000000

# Long axis trending 045
plot(ellipse_points(0, 0, a = 1, R = 3, angle = 45), type = "l", asp = 1)
